name: PHASOR
tagline: RF calculator kit: dBm converter, VSWR and return loss, interactive Smith chart, noise figure cascade and link budget
meta_description: Free RF calculator: dBm/watts/volts converter, VSWR and return loss, interactive Smith chart with L-match solver, Friis noise cascade and link budget.
description:
PHASOR is a pocket toolkit for radio-frequency engineers, students and hobbyists. It brings together the calculations you reach for every day on the bench, and it runs entirely in your browser, with nothing to install and no sign-up.

The Convert tab turns any power or voltage (dBm, dBW, watts, Vrms, Vpk, Vpp, dBµV, dBmV) into all the others at the impedance you choose. Next to it, a mismatch converter moves between VSWR, return loss, reflection coefficient, S11, mismatch loss and reflected power, with a meter showing how much power actually reaches the load.

The Smith tab is an interactive Smith chart. Drag the load point around, or type its resistance and reactance, and PHASOR solves every two-element L-network that matches it to your system impedance. It gives real inductor and capacitor values at your frequency and draws each matching path on the chart.

The Cascade tab works out a receiver chain's total gain, noise figure (Friis), input and output IP3, sensitivity and spurious-free dynamic range. It also shows how much of the total noise each stage contributes. The Link tab builds a free-space link budget with a waterfall chart, fade margin, maximum range and Fresnel-zone radius. Your values are saved on your device.
how_to: Pick a tab: Convert, Smith, Cascade or Link.
Type your values. Every result updates as you type.
On the Smith chart, drag the load point and tap a match solution to see its path.
Tap any result tile to copy its value.
Open the '?' notes under each panel for the formulas behind the numbers.

name: Gyre
tagline: Euclidean rhythm machine: four rings of synthesized drums that spread beats evenly and drift into polyrhythms
meta_description: Free online Euclidean rhythm generator and drum machine. Build polyrhythms with four rotating rings, tresillo and bembé presets, swing and tempo control.
description:
Gyre is a playable Euclidean rhythm machine that runs in your browser. Four concentric rings (hi-hat, chime, snare and kick) each spread a chosen number of hits across a chosen number of steps as evenly as possible. This is the Euclidean algorithm, and it turns out to produce many of the world's traditional rhythms.

Set a ring to 3 hits over 8 steps and you get the Cuban tresillo. 5 over 8 gives the cinquillo, and 7 over 12 gives the West African bembé bell pattern. Give the rings different step counts and they loop at different lengths, so the groove keeps shifting against itself until the cycles line up again. Gyre shows that cycle length in the middle of the dial.

Every sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API, so there are no samples to download. Rotate any ring to shift its pattern, tap individual dots to break the rule, add swing, and save your groove automatically on your device. It's a quick way to explore rhythm theory, find ideas for a beat, or just watch the patterns orbit.
how_to: Press Play (or the space bar) to start the beat.
Pick a preset such as Tresillo, Bembé or Odd 7·9·11, or press Shuffle.
Use each ring's Steps, Hits and Rotate sliders to change its pattern.
Tap any dot on the dial to flip that single step on or off.
Adjust Tempo and Swing, and mute rings to hear the layers.

name: Mycel
tagline: Rotate-the-tiles connection puzzle: turn fungus strands until every mushroom links to the glowing spore
meta_description: Free daily pipe-rotation puzzle game in your browser. Turn the tiles to connect every mushroom to the spore. 5×5, 7×7 and 9×9 boards, daily and random modes.
description:
Mycel is a calm, glowing take on the classic rotate-the-pipes connection puzzle. The board is a patch of forest floor crossed by strands of fungus. A spore sits in the middle, and mushrooms are scattered at the ends of the strands. Every tile has been turned at random, and your job is to rotate them back until every mushroom draws food from the spore.

Tap a tile to turn it a quarter clockwise. Strands that connect back to the spore light up amber, so you can watch the network grow as you solve it. Long-press (or right-click) a tile you're sure of to pin it so you can't turn it by accident. When the last mushroom is fed, a wave of light ripples outward across the board.

Choose a 5×5 Patch, 7×7 Grove or 9×9 Forest. Daily mode gives everyone the same board each day, and Wild mode makes a fresh random board whenever you like. Your best time and move count for each size are saved on your device. There's no sign-up and no ads, and it works on phones and desktops.
how_to: Tap a tile to rotate it clockwise.
Connect strands back to the glowing spore in the middle. Connected strands light up.
Long-press or right-click a tile to pin it in place.
Feed every mushroom to finish the board.
Switch size, or press New for a random Wild board.
